prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Create ONE square 1024x1024 detailed painterly naturalistic encyclopedia illustration of the LERNAEAN HYDRA in the nine-headed variant documented by Apollodorus, Library 2.5.2. A huge truly SERPENTINE water monster in a dark Greek marsh, one massive limbless coiled snake body and EXACTLY NINE independently visible snake heads, each on its own long sinuous neck attached to the same body. Make nine heads immediately countable and not overlapping: a central upright snake head, four fanning clearly on its left and four on its right. Eight mortal heads and the central immortal head; all are snake heads, no invented crowns. One continuous heavy coiled tail. Venomous open jaws and glistening dark wet scales; reed beds, black still water and mist behind. Ancient monstrous menace and poisonous horror, oppressive dawn light with restrained natural color. Entire silhouette comfortably inside frame, detailed naturalistic snake anatomy and exquisite oil brush texture. No legs, arms, wings, horns, dragon heads, dinosaur body, extra head, tenth head, missing head, flame breath, bright fantasy magic, humans, corpses, labels, text, watermark or border. Nine heads exactly.
Critical correction: prior composition had only SEVEN heads and must be rejected. This new image MUST contain NINE visible heads, no exceptions. Arrange the nine heads at separately spaced positions across the upper frame, like nine upright snake necks in a gently curved row: count 1,2,3,4 left of center, head 5 at center, heads 6,7,8,9 right of center. Every one has its own face and neck, clearly separated by empty background. Keep the body lower in the frame so there is generous room for all nine faces. Head count is the highest-priority invariant.
visual_requirements: Exactly nine snake heads, individually countable
One huge limbless coiled serpent body
Venomous threatening monster in Greek marsh
depicted_variant: Apollodorus nine-headed serpent, eight mortal and central immortal

visual_review.notes: Counted nine separate open snake heads: four left of central head, central head, four right. Each has its own long neck joining the mass of one scaled coiled serpent; no legs or wings. Large exposed venomous fangs, bleak misty marsh, wet black scales and menacing raised mouths convey dangerous horror. Earlier seven-headed file was deleted before regeneration.
